# Independent review: exact source generator and existing SUPPORT

Date: 2026-09-17.
Reviewer: /root/pairzero_geometry_review.
Verdict: ACCEPT_EXACT_SOURCE_GENERATOR_SUPPORT_EQUIVALENCE_ONLY.
Disposition: A1--A6 accepted; no mathematical correction required.
Classification: DOMAIN_AND_ALIAS_AUDIT_ONLY.

## 1. Exact candidate and task boundary

Candidate: `SOURCE_GENERATOR_SUPPORT_AUDIT.md`.
SHA256: `8fa7f3b681732de1c784127178b0e438cc5bbc1950660a6df3f0514abd622f95`.
Bytes: 10909. LF: 239.
Recorded isolated source base: `7dcc9c210791f12dc419a0db3d3957185a6cb191`.

The complete candidate was read. The relevant named sections of its six
pinned source inputs were read directly, and all six complete-file hashes
were recomputed and matched. This is a bounded audit of normalization,
operator domains, the graph core, and the exact alias with old SUPPORT.
It is not a new proof of either sign of full V, a new positive mechanism,
or a new source-support proof. No previous task is reopened by this review.

Only this staging review file is written. No search, external theorem
import, descendant agent, Pro dispatch, repository/control/queue change,
publication, numerical theta scan, or Lean run is part of this review.

## 2. Source reconciliation

All paths below are the named files in `docs/Codex` of the specified
`gamma-reciprocity-worktree`.

1. `REPORT_2026-09-12_FULL_SIGN_TRANSFER_AUDIT.md`:
   `1e296a504631b58beb7863f4c7f36174bd08876cfc7093febfe00cc8306a5282`.
   Lines 15--23 fix the complete theta source and A=||Phi||_2;

2. `REPORT_2026-09-15_FULLVPOS_INTAKE.md`:
   `8f9abe3e60ce3188709ad5b6e91022980a78bc33f70635fcb4f3fe6abb77aad6`.
   Lines 39--48 identify E=F+iF', S=(F-iF')/(F+iF') and the exact unitary U.
   Lines 69--89 give the already accepted all-row V / SUPPORT equivalence.
   Lines 98--107 give the Gaussian and non-theta negative controls.

3. `REPORT_2026-09-15_SOURCE_SUPPORT_HUNT.md`:
   `9b059659b10948bed90d9df482cfe97e9cc229116e1db46b029bba81a22c4966`.
   Lines 16--24 fix the same source, Fourier sign, I, and SUPPORT direction;

4. `REPORT_2026-09-17_CONDITIONAL_CONNECTION.md`:
   `2aa3c9dcd948045ee21dbc0f530fa73037968dce40d8c4592bedd48aed1757c9`.
   Lines 122--140 preserve the full scalar flux, the mixed term, and the

5. `REPORT_2026-09-14_FULL_V_RANK_TWO_INTAKE.md`:
   `51168fb802d7facfb74291d0a3fc0009b121f540711df2fe10ae01cd84c1d14f`.
   Lines 148--201 establish the distinct control f0, its exact negative
   jet -25/162, and genuine finite negative rows inside the original I.
   No explicit numeric h and no negative theta row were asserted there.

6. `REPORT_2026-09-15_SUPPORTSTABILITY_INTAKE.md`:
   `14f8e48fd325f41df7b46f1da84140e1ff56b16df95ee3c6b9c0000f9ae9e895`.
   Lines 91--125 give p in L2 iff W2 iff SUPPORT iff all-row V>=0.
   Lines 127--147 retain the response boundary and distinguish controls;
   lines 160--163 record the requested return before another expansion
   of the same unweighted-response obligation.

The candidate's source-phase orientation and statement that the proposed
commutator route returns to the old target match these exact inputs.

## 3. A1--A2: normalization, signs, maximal domain, and the exact form

PASS; candidate lines 16--73.

With the nonunitary Fourier integral F(omega)=int f(t)exp(-i omega t)dt,
Plancherel has frequency measure domega/(2pi), as stated. The Mellin
normalization is F(z)=xi(1/2-iz)/A, with no additional factor of two or
square root of 2pi. Real even f gives real even F on the real line;
the full real double-exponential tails make F entire. Since F(0)>0,
its real zeros are isolated and have Lebesgue measure zero. Neither RH
nor simplicity of these zeros is needed.

The exact Fourier identities are

    Fourier[f(t+x)] = exp(i omega x) F(omega),
    Fourier[(t+x)f(t+x)] = i exp(i omega x) F'(omega).

Thus the maximal multiplier B=i m, m=F'/F real a.e., has precisely the
source relation B u_x=w_x. Here F' belongs to L2 by the full source tails
and Plancherel (and also by A5), so every u_x lies in Dom(B). Changing m
at isolated zeros changes neither its operator nor its maximal domain.
The actual poles near real zeros remain paid for by the domain condition.

A real measurable finite-a.e. multiplier is self-adjoint on its maximal
domain: testing the adjoint on sets with bounded m identifies that same
maximal domain. Consequently B is densely defined, closed, skew-adjoint.
This statement has no zero-free or bounded-multiplier premise.

For a finite complex coefficient row, taking twice the real part of the
half-line pairing symmetrizes t+x_j with t+x_i. It gives exactly the full
kernel factor 2t+x_i+x_j, hence V[c]=2 Re <P+u_c,Bu_c>. No cross term or
negative interval of an original shifted signal is deleted.

The form b(u,v)=<P+u,Bv>+<Bu,P+v> is Hermitian and bounded by
||u||||Bv||+||Bu||||v||, hence graph-norm continuous on Dom(B). Only when
BP+ is defined may it be written as an operator commutator [P+,B]. The
candidate correctly works with the form and never uses the false general
assertion P+Dom(B) contained in Dom(B). B acts on the full-line translated
source, so the former half-line common-multiplier obstruction is not being
contradicted or bypassed by silently changing a domain.

## 4. A3: exponential moments and the graph core on the original I

PASS; candidate lines 80--119.

For positive omega, shifting t to Im t=-delta multiplies the Fourier
integrand by exp(-delta omega); for negative omega the upward shift gives
exp(-delta|omega|). The same shift for F' carries the factor -it and is
therefore bounded by the horizontal integral of |t f(t)|. The complete
theta expansion on Re t>=0 has cos(2 Im t)>=cos(2delta)>0. Its full sum,
including the polynomial prefactors, has uniform double-exponential tails.
Evenness supplies the other side. These facts pay both vertical contours
and both horizontal weighted integrals. They justify the claimed common
bound for |F|+|F'| without an asymptotic formula for F'/F.

The measure mu=(|F|^2+|F'|^2)domega/(2pi) is finite and satisfies
int exp(2eta|omega|)dmu<infinity for eta<delta. Multiplication q -> Fq
is an isometric surjection from L2(mu) onto Dom(B) in the graph norm:

    ||u||^2+||Bu||^2 = int (|F|^2+|F'|^2)|q|^2 domega/(2pi).

Surjectivity is correctly checked by q=hat(u)/F a.e. The null set of real
zeros supports no missing L2 component; no bounded inverse multiplication
on the unweighted Fourier space is asserted.

If q is orthogonal to exp(i omega x) for all x in I, then
nu=conj(q)mu has an exponential eta moment by Cauchy--Schwarz. Its transform
int exp(i omega z)dnu is holomorphic on |Im z|<eta. On compact smaller
strips the extra powers of omega required for derivatives are absorbed
by the remaining exponential margin. Vanishing on the real interval I
therefore implies vanishing on the entire strip, then Fourier uniqueness
for finite measures yields nu=0 and q=0 mu-a.e.

Accordingly span{u_x:x in I} is a graph core, not merely L2-dense. By the
continuity of b, positivity on all its finite complex combinations is
equivalent to b[u]>=0 throughout Dom(B). This is a valid equivalence,
not a proof of positivity of either side.

## 5. A4: correct direction of support and energy monotonicity

PASS; candidate lines 123--144.

The multiplier exp(-i tau m) defines a strongly continuous unitary group.
It preserves Dom(B) because its modulus is one and commutes there with B.
The dominated difference quotient, bounded by |m| times |hat(u)|, gives
T'_tau u=-B T_tau u for u in Dom(B). Therefore

    d/dtau ||P+T_tau u||^2 = -b[T_tau u].

If b is nonnegative, the projected norm is nonincreasing for tau>=0.
Density of Dom(B) extends the resulting bounded-operator inequality to
all of H. Starting with u in H- gives T_tau u in H-.

Conversely, if T_tau preserves H- for every nonnegative tau, decompose
u=P+u+P-u. The negative component has zero projected output, so unitarity
yields ||P+T_tau u||<=||P+u||. For u in Dom(B), its right derivative at
zero is -b[u], proving b[u]>=0. Applying the same inequality to T_su also
recovers monotonicity at later s. No claim that P+u itself lies in Dom(B)
is required in this direction either.

The forward half-line is negative support, and the positive time flow is
e^{-tau B}. These signs are consistent with the source-phase convention.
Unitarity by itself would not supply this support preservation.

## 6. A5: exact old Cayley transform and both implications

PASS; candidate lines 148--189.

For real frequencies away from the null zero set,

    (1-i m)/(1+i m)=(F-iF')/(F+iF')=S.

Thus the exact operator identity is U=(1-B)(1+B)^{-1}, not U^{-1}.
The inverse (1+B)^{-1} maps all H into Dom(B): both 1/(1+i m) and
m/(1+i m) are bounded. At real zeros the old phase's removable-value
convention and the arbitrary definition of m can differ only on a null
set, which leaves the L2 operator identity intact.

For each u, the Bochner integral int_0^infinity e^{-tau}T_tau u dtau is
norm convergent and has multiplier 1/(1+i m), proving the stated
resolvent formula. If every T_tau preserves closed H-, that resolvent
and U=2(1+B)^{-1}-1 preserve H-.

For the reverse direction, h_tau(w)=exp[-tau(1-w)/(1+w)] is holomorphic
and bounded by one on the open disk for tau>=0. For r<1, its power series
at rU converges in operator norm. Only nonnegative powers of U occur, so
invariance of H- under U suffices; no invariance under U* is assumed.

For a.e. omega, m is finite and S=(1-i m)/(1+i m) is not -1. Therefore

    (1-S)/(1+S)=i m,
    h_tau(rS) -> exp(-i tau m).

The uniform bound one and dominated convergence against |hat(u)|^2 give
strong convergence h_tau(rU)u -> T_tau u. Closedness of H- passes
invariance to T_tau. Values at the isolated source zeros do not affect
this limit. For tau=0 the constant function h_0=1 gives the same result.

Consequently the support law for the full unitary flow is precisely
U(H-) contained in H-, equivalently P+UP-=0. The six pinned source inputs
identify this as old SUPPORT, and then as old unweighted W2 / p-in-L2.
No inverse phase, norm change, weaker quantifier, or new source criterion
is substituted in this comparison.

## 7. A6: exact Gaussian boundary and negative control

PASS; candidate lines 191--224.

For f_a(t)=exp(-a t^2), F'/F=-omega/(2a). Since Fourier[partial_t u]
=i omega hat(u), the exact generator is B=-(1/(2a))partial_t and
T_tau u(t)=u(t+tau/(2a)). This moves negative support left, as required.
For the smooth decaying finite source rows,

    b[u]=-Re int_0^infinity conj(u)u' dt / a
        =|u(0)|^2/(2a).

The factor and sign agree with the exact Gaussian kernel V_a(x,y)=
f_a(x)f_a(y)/(2a). The answer is a physical boundary contribution, not
zero. Indeed, a function with nonzero trace at zero generally leaves the
H1 derivative domain after multiplication by P+, confirming why the
form-domain formulation was needed.

For f0=exp(-t^2)-exp(-2t^2)/4, real evenness, isolated Fourier zeros and
Gaussian strip tails give the same maximal multiplier and graph-core
construction. The already accepted four-shift negative row lies inside
I for sufficiently small h. By the proved equivalences it forces failure
of support preservation for this control. The argument does not assume
that f0 shares the theta source's weighted-Schur property; the source
inputs explicitly distinguish that issue.

Thus the controls correctly show that exact input/output matching,
skew-adjointness, unitarity, graph-core density and scalar evenness do not
settle SUPPORT. There is no negative row or failed support vector for the
actual theta source in this audit.

## Final disposition

ACCEPT_EXACT_SOURCE_GENERATOR_SUPPORT_EQUIVALENCE_ONLY.

The domain and graph-core issues are paid, the reverse Cayley implication
is valid, and the exact source phase and half-line orientation are
preserved. The completed chain is

    original all-finite V>=0 on I
      iff b>=0 on Dom(B)
      iff exp(-tau B) preserves H- for all tau>=0
      iff the OLD U preserves H-
      iff OLD SUPPORT.

This is an exact domain/alias audit. It supplies no new positive energy
reserve, source-specific sign mechanism, improved bound, or RH proof.
It does not justify redispatching the same unresolved SUPPORT request
under a flow or commutator name. Full V positivity and RH remain open.

# Parent check of source generator audit

Candidate: SOURCE_GENERATOR_SUPPORT_AUDIT.md
SHA256: 8fa7f3b681732de1c784127178b0e438cc5bbc1950660a6df3f0514abd622f95

- With exp(-i omega t), Fourier[t f]=i Fprime and translation f(t+x) contributes exp(i omega x). Hence B u_x=w_x; there is no extra x term in this centered output.
- m real a.e. defines the maximal skew-adjoint multiplier B even when real F zeros have any multiplicity. Real zero sets are null, but poles still determine Dom(B).
- Graph norm equals the L2 norm of q against (F^2+Fprime^2)domega/(2pi), where uhat=F q. The map is onto almost everywhere; graph density follows from strip analytic uniqueness, using the source strip only, without any Fourier zero-free hypothesis.
- Projection P+ is bounded on H but is not claimed graph bounded. All calculations use the two-variable form; no distributional boundary term is discarded by an unjustified operator commutator.
- Ttau=exp(-tau B): the energy derivative is minus b. Nonnegative b implies negative support is forward invariant; conversely invariance and unitarity imply P+ energy contraction and the right derivative gives b nonnegative.
- Cayley S=(1-i m)/(1+i m) matches the old phase U. The resolvent Laplace integral and the disk function exp[-tau(1-w)/(1+w)] give both directions of support equivalence. A point S=-1 occurs only on a null set, so the strong boundary limit is valid.
- Gaussian: B=-partial_t/(2a), forward evolution u(t+tau/(2a)), b=|u(0)|^2/(2a). This independently fixes sign, support orientation and factor two.
- Negative f0 control meets the same construction and density assumptions. Therefore the unconditional generator and its unitarity cannot give the missing one-sided support.

The result is an exact domain/alias audit of an old target, not a new sign bound, proof route, counterexample to theta V, or a reset of the repeated-obstacle history.

Source note: FULL_SIGN_TRANSFER pins normalization and real tails; FULLVPOS explicitly supplies holomorphic strip continuation, and A3 also writes the full-mode contour justification directly. No unseen source is attributed an independent positivity theorem.
accepted: A1--A2: maximal skew-adjoint full-source Fourier generator B realizes Bu_x=w_x and its cutoff Hermitian form equals original full V
A3: admissible translates on I form a graph core for B; all-row V positivity is equivalent to b>=0 on Dom(B)
A4: b>=0 is equivalent to negative-half-line invariance under the explicit unitary flow exp(-tau B) for every tau>=0
A5: the Cayley transform of B is precisely the old FULLVPOS U and has the same half-line support condition
A6: Gaussian factors and support direction match, while the accepted non-theta negative control rules out generic unitarity as a sign proof
domain_limits: B acts on full-line source translates before P+; not the excluded zero-extended half-line common multiplier
P+Dom(B) subset Dom(B) is not asserted; the commutator is a graph-continuous form
real zero poles enter the maximal multiplier domain; real zero sets are ignored only as null sets
neither bounded inverse synthesis nor any location or simplicity of xi zeros is assumed
decision_effect: Do not redispatch the existing SUPPORT target under positive commutator, unitary propagation, causal flow or conserved full-line energy without a new source-specific premise. This audit supplies no such premise.
